en: <Color:255,200,200,255>What's the point if I'm not interested? I start things because I want to make friends, not because I like the thing itself.
So for you, hobbies don't go beyond forging connections with people? That strikes me as missing something.
Noodles?
<Color:255,200,200,255>Yeah, he was in the band. Don't ask me any more about it.<Color:Default>
<Color:255,200,200,255>So yeah, I do lots of different stuff.<Color:Default>
Hey, Kiryu-san? Do you have rules on when you decide to take a relationship to an intimate level?<Color:Default>
You're full of tough questions, aren't you?
<Color:255,200,200,255>Us girls need to plan for that sort of thing, you know? Stuff like, "Hey, would I be okay having this guy's kid?" and whatnot.<Color:Default>
I'd consider marriage. Otherwise, it's a no-go for me. That's a man's responsibility.
<Color:255,200,200,255>You've really thought about this, haven't you?<Color:Default>
At my age, you kind of have to.
It's not about kids. If you love somebody, that should be enough.
<Color:255,200,200,255>Right? I suppose guys all think like that, though.<Color:Default>
If you're capable of risk management, there won't be issues if things go too far.
It depends on how things feel. I'm not built to think too far into the future.
<Color:255,200,200,255>Yeah, younger men are like that a lot. I guess you're like that, too.<Color:Default>
I'm a man, after all.
<Color:255,200,200,255>I can only talk about stuff like this with you, Kiryu-san.<Color:Default>
Why just with me?
<Color:255,200,200,255>With other people, even when the talk gets serious, things turn to sex right away.<Color:Default>
<Color:255,200,200,255>But I like you because you always hear me out seriously!<Color:Default>
I'm used to being counted on. As an older person, it's my role to guide younger people.
<Color:255,200,200,255>Um, okay then. While we're at it, I have a question for you. Straight up, what do you think about me?<Color:Default>
<Color:255,200,200,255>Would you marry me, then?<Color:Default>
Whoa, I haven't thought about it that much.
<Color:255,200,200,255>Hmm...<Color:Default>
<Color:255,200,200,255>Then I guess it'd be okay for us to date! I can't stand the thought of dating a guy if I think there'll be some drama further down the line.<Color:Default>
I guess I should be happy about that.
<Color:255,200,200,255>But you haven't thought about having kids?<Color:Default>
Of course not. That would be rushing things, don't you think?
<Color:255,200,200,255>Hmmm...<Color:Default>
I suppose I should be happy about that.
<Color:255,200,200,255>So then, depending on the mood, would you want to do sexual stuff with me?<Color:Default>
Only if you wanted to. If the girl makes the first move, I'm not going to say no.
<Color:255,200,200,255>I guess we couldn't date, then. I feel like there'd just be drama further down the line.<Color:Default>
You're complicated. Everyone has problems big and small, but I don't think I've ever met someone as stubborn as you.
<Color:255,200,200,255>Hahaha! You really think so?<Color:Default>
<Color:255,200,200,255>Because I like people who are honest! Knowing when to be polite is all well and good, but I like it when someone knows to speak their mind.<Color:Default>
That's what I like about you, too.
I'm like any other man. Being subjected to this kind of unguarded, frank confessional talk makes me feel like you don't see me that way.
<Color:255,200,200,255>Oh, no. It's not like that, really.<Color:Default>
<Color:255,200,200,255>With you, Kiryu-san, I feel like even if things did go in that direction, I wouldn't mind because it's you.<Color:Default>
I feel the same way. I get the sense that things would work out well between us.
You too? Maybe we really are compatible!<Color:Default>
I don't know about that. I'm still a guy. I might talk a good game, but who knows what could happen when the actual time comes?
<Color:255,200,200,255>Oh, that actually makes me feel better! It's the guys who insist up and down that they're trustworthy that you have to look out for!<Color:Default>
Is that how it goes?
Want to give it a shot?
<Color:255,200,200,255>See, why'd you have to go there!? Didn't I just tell you I didn't like that sort of talk?<Color:Default>
Oh, sorry...
<Color:255,200,200,255>Ugh, this bites.<Color:Default>
What's Kamurocho like these days? There doesn't seem to be as many people around anymore.
Yeah, a lot of stuff happened last year. Even the cabaret club clientele seems to have moved on to greener pastures.
That's too bad. This neighborhood used to be a bastion of chaos, a tinge of danger always hanging in the air.
...Right. Well, now there's just a bunch of empty buildings.
They'll have signs up in the day, but if you go there at night, they're not open. There's only notices saying they've closed down.
Really? Things are worse than I imagined.
But maybe that's for the best. Kamurocho Hills being built is a sign the area's changing. Maybe there'll be more ordinary customers now.
No, it's not good at all! The economy's awful, so everyone's even more desperate than before. Creeps like club recruiters and barkers are just the worst now!
I'm usually in a hurry to get to work, so I wish they'd leave me alone!
Right. The bad ones won't even let you pass.
Yeah, I hate it. I take underground tunnels all the way from the station. I barely even know the layout of the surface streets.
I always thought the world of a hostess would be more glamorous, but it really is quite plain.
Maybe I'm better off trying to make my way in a flashier city, like Osaka or Nagoya.
Not a bad idea. I hear Osaka is still doing pretty well.
Really!? Do you hit up all the trendy clubs in places like that, Kiryu-san?
Of course I do. Over the years I've had business all over the country, so I make sure to hit up the local cabaret clubs when I'm in town.
That's amazing! I wish everyone was more of a big player like you, Kiryu-san!
Are you complimenting me, or...?
I prefer when it's less busy. Empty clubs make it easier to get friendly with a girl.
Haha, I hear that! You have no competition, and the girls are super happy to see you.
Still, this club is doing pretty well. There aren't many like this in Tokyo.
It's the same everywhere. It's not only Kamurocho that's in a recession⑬it's all of Japan.
Aww. Why'd I have the rotten luck of hitting adulthood at such a lousy time?
I wish I'd gotten to experience the bubble economy like you did, Kiryu-san.
Now you sound like an old-timer. You just need to work at it harder, that's all.
Greener pastures?
You know, like Ginza or Roppongi. Lots of girls have moved out to places like that.
That's sad to hear. I wish more people shared my affection for this part of town.
It can't be helped! Everyone's got to make a living, so of course they're going to go where the money is.
I understand that. But for me, this is the city where all my dreams were formed.
If this place dies out, I feel I may as well fade along with it.
Wow, Kiryu-san. You really do love Kamurocho, don't you?
I wasn't aware. I figured those places were full of high-end clubs that only big spenders could afford.
There are lots of clubs like that, but there are plenty of affordable ones, too. It's sort of like Kamurocho not too long ago.
I see. Maybe I should check it out sometime.
Will you go, too?
I don't know. Kamurocho is an easier commute from my house.
I hang out around here a lot too, and it's nice to be able to have fun with friends before work.
Good point. Your personal life is important too.
Will you be at the club on Christmas Eve?
Why do you ask?
Just curious.
Unfortunately, I'm off that day.
Are you disappointed?
Kind of.
Haha! You don't need to be that upset! I'm only going to see a concert!
Oh, is that all?
Should I be?
Oh, come on! You can't hide your disappointment from me! Maybe you should just try to make your own plans.
You're lying. I bet you don't have any plans, you're just trying to make it seem that way.
I do have plans, honest! And I need the money, so if I had the time I'd definitely be here!
Besides, if a hostess works on Christmas Eve, it's a sign she's not popular.
Well, sure. Girls with regular clients would only come in after some extravagant dinner, and ones with boyfriends wouldn't even be here.
So if you were to come to the club, you'd be stuck with girls who are leftovers.
That's not good. When I come to a cabaret club, it's because I want to forget about my real life for a while.
Hehe. If it bugs you that much, then you should visit our club more! That way you'll have a girl you can invite out on Christmas Eve.
What's wrong with that? If circumstances bring the "losers" together, they'll already have something in common. They might even become friends.
I've never thought about it that way! But since you'd be an important client, I'm sure you'd still get excellent service.
So does this mean that you're free on Christmas Eve, Kiryu-san?
Kind of. I'm not really a party guy, but drinking alone on a night like that...
I figured you'd have at least one or two girls to spend time with. Why don't you?
Heh. Wish I knew.
Not really. Of course I have plans. I only wanted to confirm your schedule.
Liar! I bet you anything you're alone that night, Kiryu-san! If you had a girlfriend, you'd never have asked!
Well, hey, this isn't about me.
That's not true. I bet some girls celebrate on another day, so they can work on Christmas Eve.
I bet! They'll probably say stuff like, "Oh, I'm all alone on Christmas Eve!" while they've actually got a date on the 23rd.
Maybe I should try that myself this year. Then I could have an extra day of work.
Seriously? Then I'm not coming on that day.
Are you sure about that? If you get lonely that evening, won't you want to see me?
Hmph. I'm not sure what you're talking about.
Don't do that. Men will just assume you don't have a life.
Whoa, true. I don't want to seem like a leftover.
It's a choice between money and pride, really.
Don't you have a concert to go to? You can't exactly move that to a different day.
Oh, you're right!
It's been a while since I've been back in Tokyo, but the girls here really are on a higher level.
What? That's not true! There are only a small number of cute girls here.
Must be my imagination. But I wonder why? What is it about Tokyo that makes me think that?
Yeah, I think there's something about the city.
If you had a girl pose against a city background and a countryside background, don't you think the city girl would seem more fashionable?
Sure, it would definitely give off a different impression.
No, it's true. I've seen girls from all over Japan, and there's nothing like the ones here.
Wow, really? But people come to Tokyo from all over the country. How can you tell them apart from the local girls?
Hm. I suppose that's a good point.
I guess what I really mean, is that Tokyo girls give off a certain air of professionalism.
No, that's not true. No way.
Everyone here's self-centered and two-faced. Nobody even knows how to speak polite Japanese.
Really? Most girls I've met aren't like that at all.
Haha! Oh, Kiryu-san, you're so innocent! That's adorable!
Am I innocent?
That can't be true. They get the job done, so they must be responsible. Not anyone can manage that sort of thing.
Nah, it's all an act. They throw themselves into their work so hard because they have to, not because they're normally kind and polite.
So, Kiryu-san, does that mean you prefer city girls?
Yeah. Being around country girls is relaxing, but it's not like the thrill you get from a hostess.
I much prefer drinking with a girl who's worldly and quick-witted.
I see! Then I guess I'll need to kick it up a notch for you!
Heh. Please do.
No. City girls tend to make me feel like I'm not up to par with them.
I like a girl who lets me take the lead, and who's a bit more exotic.
Oh, I see. So, I guess I should keep quiet and not start conversations with you?
No, wait...
I like both. Everyone's got their good and bad sides. If you focus on the good side, both types of girls are appealing.
Haha, you're quite the smooth talker!
You're right, though. Like, I wouldn't be able to pick my preference between clients from   Tokyo, or ones from the country.
